question: Which combination vehicle requires a Class A CDL?
choice_a: Any combination with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) is more than 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Any combination with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the towed vehicle(s) is 10,000 pounds or less
choice_c: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_d: Any vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers
explanation: The manual defines Class A as any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Classifications

question: A single straight vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR, falls into which class?
explanation: Class B Heavy Straight Vehicles are any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or any such vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Classifications

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds is Class C, but requires a CDL only if it also meets which condition?
choice_a: It has more than two axles
choice_b: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers (including the driver), or it hauls hazardous materials requiring placarding
choice_d: It is used exclusively in interstate commerce
explanation: Class C vehicles are included in the CDL program only if designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials in quantities requiring placarding (or select agents/toxins).
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Classifications

question: A driver who holds a Class A CDL is, according to the manual, also qualified to drive vehicles in which other classes?
choice_c: Both Class B and Class C
choice_d: Neither Class B nor Class C
explanation: Since Class A driving skills include those required for Class B and C, a driver with a Class A license may also drive vehicles in Classes B and C.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Classifications

question: A CDL is required for a vehicle designed to transport how many or more passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual states a CDL is required to operate a vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction

question: The Double and Triple Trailers (T) endorsement, for drivers who wish to pull multiple trailers, applies to drivers qualified for which class of vehicle?
explanation: The manual states that drivers qualified to drive Class A vehicles who wish to pull double or triple trailers must add the T endorsement.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required when a tank has an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons?
explanation: The N endorsement applies to tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: Besides the individual tank capacity threshold, the Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement also applies when the tank's aggregate rated capacity is what amount or more?
explanation: The N endorsement is required for tanks with an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more that are permanently or temporarily attached to the vehicle or chassis.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: A Passenger (P) endorsement is required for a vehicle with a design capacity to carry how many or more people, including the driver?
explanation: Drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity of 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a passenger endorsement.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: Drivers seeking a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement must undergo which additional federal requirement?
choice_a: A TSA background check that reviews criminal, immigration, and FBI records
choice_b: A separate CDL road test conducted only in a hazmat-loaded vehicle
choice_c: A minimum of five years of driving experience
choice_d: Certification from the Environmental Protection Agency
explanation: The TSA and US DOT require background checks, including review of criminal, immigration, and FBI records, for drivers certified to transport hazardous materials.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: The Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X) endorsement is required for drivers who:
choice_a: Haul only empty, purged tank vehicles
choice_b: Haul hazardous materials or waste in tank vehicles in amounts requiring placards
choice_c: Drive school buses that occasionally carry small packages
choice_d: Pull double trailers carrying dry freight
explanation: Drivers of tank vehicles who haul hazardous materials or waste in amounts requiring placards must add an X endorsement, showing they passed the special exams for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Endorsements

question: According to the manual, how many standardized restriction codes exist that may be added to a CDL or CLP?
explanation: The manual states there are ten standardized restriction codes based on the type of vehicle and equipment used for the skills test.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, which restriction is placed on the CDL?
choice_a: (Z) - No full air brake equipped CMV
explanation: If the skills test is performed in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, the state must indicate on the CDL that the person is restricted from operating a CMV with a manual transmission -- the (E) restriction.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: The (K) restriction limits a CDL holder to which type of operation?
explanation: If an applicant certifies as Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate, the state must indicate the (K) restriction, showing the person is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: A driver who does not take or fails the air brake component of the knowledge test, or who tests in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes, will receive which restriction?
explanation: The (L) restriction -- No air brake equipped CMV -- applies when an applicant does not take or fails the air brake knowledge test component, or tests in a vehicle without air brakes.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: The (O) restriction -- No tractor trailer CMV -- applies when a Group A skills test is passed in a combination vehicle connected by what?
choice_b: A pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection
explanation: If the skills test for a Group A CDL is performed in a combination vehicle with the power unit and towed unit connected by a pintle hook or other non-fifth-wheel connection, the (O) restriction applies.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: The (V) restriction code on a CDL indicates what?
choice_a: The driver holds only a vision waiver
choice_b: The existence of a medical variance noted on the driver's CDLIS record
choice_c: The driver failed the vehicle inspection segment of the skills test
choice_d: The driver is restricted to vehicles under 10,000 pounds GVWR
explanation: If the state is notified that a driver has been issued a medical variance, the state must indicate this on the CDLIS driver record and the CDL document using restriction code 'V.'
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: The (Z) restriction applies to a driver who performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with which type of brakes?
explanation: If an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with air over hydraulic brakes, the state must add the (Z) restriction, prohibiting operation of a CMV with a full air brake system.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions

question: Which endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Hazardous Materials, Tank Vehicle, and Doubles/Triples
choice_b: Passenger, School Bus, and Tank Vehicle
choice_c: Passenger, Hazardous Materials, and School Bus
explanation: The manual states the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N).
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions (CLP)

question: If a CLP is issued with a Passenger (P) or School Bus (S) endorsement, it must also carry which restriction?
choice_a: (X) - No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_b: (P) - No passengers in a CMV bus
explanation: The manual states that a CLP issued with a P or S endorsement must also contain a (P) -- No passengers in a CMV bus restriction.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions (CLP)

question: If a CLP is issued with a Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement, it must also carry which restriction?
choice_a: (X) - No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle
choice_b: (Z) - No full air brake equipped CMV
explanation: The manual states that a CLP issued with a Tanker (N) endorsement must also contain a (X) -- No cargo in a CMV tank vehicle restriction, so the CLP holder may only operate an empty, purged tank vehicle.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, CDL Endorsements & Restrictions - Restrictions (CLP)

question: Which knowledge test must be taken by all CDL applicants?
explanation: The manual lists the general knowledge test as the test taken by all applicants, regardless of the class or endorsement sought.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: The air brakes knowledge test must be taken by any applicant whose vehicle has which feature?
choice_b: Air brakes, including air over hydraulic brakes
explanation: The air brakes test must be taken if the applicant's vehicle has air brakes, including air over hydraulic brakes.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: In addition to passing the hazardous materials knowledge test, what else must an applicant do to obtain the H endorsement?
choice_a: Complete a four-year commercial driving record review
choice_b: Pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check
choice_c: Obtain a commercial driving school certificate
explanation: The manual states that to obtain the hazardous materials endorsement, an applicant is also required to pass a TSA background check.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: The passenger transport knowledge test must be taken by which applicants?
explanation: The manual lists the passenger transport test as taken by all bus driver applicants.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of which three segments, taken in order?
choice_a: Written exam, road sign test, and parallel parking
choice_b: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving
choice_c: Pre-trip inspection, air brake check, and backing
choice_d: Basic vehicle control, vehicle inspection, and highway merge
explanation: The manual states the CDL Skills Test consists of three segments: vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving, taken in that order.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: Regarding the order of the CDL skills test segments, what does the manual require?
choice_a: Segments may be taken in any order the examiner prefers
choice_b: Applicants must take the segments in the listed order and pass each one before moving to the next
choice_c: Only the on-road driving segment needs to be passed
choice_d: All three segments are scored together as a single combined result
explanation: The manual specifies applicants must take the skills test segments in the order listed and must pass each one before moving to the next.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: During the Vehicle Inspection segment of the skills test, what must an applicant do?
choice_a: State that the vehicle recently passed a state inspection
choice_b: Point to/touch and name the item being inspected and explain to the examiner what would be inspected and why
choice_c: Complete the inspection silently without speaking to the examiner
choice_d: Inspect only the tires and mirrors
explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, the applicant must point to/touch and name the item being inspected and explain to the examiner what would be inspected and why.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: What restriction applies to vehicles used for the CDL Skills Test?
choice_a: The vehicle must be less than one year old
choice_b: Any vehicle that has components marked or labeled cannot be used
choice_c: The vehicle must have a manual transmission
choice_d: The vehicle must be owned by the state licensing agency
explanation: The manual states any vehicle that has components marked or labeled cannot be used for the CDL Skills Test.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: Per the manual, drivers applying for, renewing, or transferring a CDL were required to begin providing commercial vehicle operation information to their State Driver's License Agency (SDLA) within what window?
choice_a: Starting January 30, 2012 and no later than January 30, 2014
choice_b: Starting January 1, 2000 and no later than January 1, 2005
choice_d: There is no specified date window
explanation: The manual states this requirement began January 30, 2012 and applied no later than January 30, 2014 for applicants renewing, upgrading, adding endorsements, or transferring a CDL.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.2 Medical Documentation Requirements

question: What happens if a driver required to have 'certified' medical status fails to provide and keep an up-to-date medical examiner's certificate?
choice_a: Nothing changes as long as the driver still holds a valid CDL
choice_b: The driver becomes 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL
choice_c: The driver is automatically downgraded to Class C only
choice_d: The driver must retake only the skills test
explanation: If a driver required to have certified medical status fails to keep the medical examiner's certificate up to date, they become 'not-certified' and may lose their CDL.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.2 Medical Documentation Requirements

question: Which of the following is one of the manual's defining scenarios for 'interstate commerce'?
choice_b: Driving a CMV from one State to another State or a foreign country
choice_d: Driving a vehicle owned by an out-of-state company, regardless of route
explanation: Interstate commerce includes driving a CMV from one State to another State or a foreign country, among other defined scenarios.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.2.1 Interstate or Intrastate Commerce

question: A driver who operates in non-excepted interstate commerce is required to provide which document to the SDLA?
choice_b: A current medical examiner's certificate (DOT card) under 49 CFR 391.45
choice_c: A notarized letter from their employer
explanation: Non-excepted interstate commerce drivers are required to provide a current medical examiner's certificate, commonly called a medical certificate or DOT card, under 49 CFR 391.45.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.2.2 Inter/Intrastate Commerce: Status Non-excepted or Excepted

question: How many self-certification status categories does the manual describe (e.g., interstate non-excepted, interstate excepted, etc.)?
explanation: The manual describes four self-certification categories: interstate non-excepted, interstate excepted, intrastate non-excepted, and intrastate excepted.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.2.3 Self-Certification Statements

question: It is illegal to operate a CMV if the driver's blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is what level or more?
explanation: The manual states it is illegal to operate a CMV if BAC is .04% or more, and operating a CMV is deemed consent to alcohol testing.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: For a first offense such as driving a CMV with a BAC of .04% or higher, how long will a driver lose their CDL, at minimum?
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least one year for a first offense involving BAC .04% or higher, DUI, refusing testing, or related violations.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: If a first disqualifying offense occurs while the driver is operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials, what is the minimum CDL loss?
explanation: The manual states the driver will lose their CDL for at least three years if the disqualifying offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What is the consequence of a second disqualifying offense such as a second DUI in a CMV?
choice_b: Loss of the CDL for life
choice_c: A $5,000 fine only, with no suspension
choice_d: Downgrade to a non-commercial license for 3 years
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for life for a second disqualifying offense.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: A driver found to have any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% will be:
choice_d: Required to retake only the knowledge test
explanation: The manual states a driver with any detectable amount of alcohol under .04% will be put out-of-service for 24 hours.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: Under the manual's definition of serious traffic violations, 'excessive speeding' means driving how far above the posted speed limit?
explanation: The manual defines excessive speeding as 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit, as one of the listed serious traffic violations.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: A driver who commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV will lose their CDL for at least:
explanation: The manual states the driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days for two serious traffic violations within a three-year period.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: A first violation of an out-of-service order results in a loss of CDL for at least:
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 90 days for a first violation of an out-of-service order.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.4 Violation of Out-of-Service Orders

question: Three or more violations of an out-of-service order within a ten-year period result in a CDL loss of at least:
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least three years if they have committed three or more out-of-service order violations in a ten-year period.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.4 Violation of Out-of-Service Orders

question: A first railroad-highway grade crossing violation results in a CDL loss of at least:
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.5 Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: Which of the following is listed as a railroad-highway grade crossing offense that can lead to disqualification?
choice_a: Failing to signal a lane change
choice_b: Failing to have sufficient space to drive completely through the crossing without stopping
choice_c: Driving above the posted highway speed limit
choice_d: Parking within 500 feet of a crossing
explanation: The manual lists 'failing to have sufficient space to drive completely through the crossing without stopping' among the six railroad-highway grade crossing offenses.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.5 Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: Which of the following would cause a driver to be denied or lose a hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_a: Being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
choice_d: Living in a different state than where the CDL was issued
explanation: The manual lists renouncing US citizenship as one of the grounds for denial or loss of the hazardous materials endorsement following the TSA background check.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.6 Hazardous Materials Endorsement Background Check and Disqualifications

question: A driver holding a hazardous materials endorsement must notify and surrender it to the issuing state within how many hours of a disqualifying conviction or indictment?
explanation: The manual requires a driver to notify and surrender the hazardous materials endorsement to the issuing state within 24 hours of any disqualifying conviction or indictment.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.7 Traffic Violations in Your Personal Vehicle

question: If a driver's personal vehicle license is revoked, cancelled, or suspended due to traffic control law violations (other than parking), what happens to their CDL?
choice_b: They also lose their CDL driving privileges
choice_c: They are only restricted from interstate driving
choice_d: They must retake only the knowledge test
explanation: The manual states that if a driver's personal vehicle privilege is revoked, cancelled, or suspended due to traffic control law violations, they will also lose their CDL driving privileges.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.3.7 Traffic Violations in Your Personal Vehicle

question: A driver caught holding more than one license may be fined up to how much, or jailed?
explanation: The manual states that a court may fine a driver up to $5,000 or put them in jail for holding more than one license.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: A CDL holder must notify their employer of a conviction for any traffic violation (except parking) within how many days?
explanation: The manual requires a driver to notify their employer within 30 days of conviction for any traffic violation except parking, regardless of vehicle type.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: Under the rules described in the manual, a CDL holder is prohibited from doing what while driving?
choice_b: Holding a mobile telephone to conduct a voice call or dialing it by pressing more than a single button
explanation: The manual prohibits holding a mobile phone to conduct a voice call or dialing by pressing more than a single button while driving, as well as texting.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: According to the manual, a driver who does not wear a safety belt is how many times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle in a crash?
explanation: The manual states that if a driver does not wear a safety belt, they are four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.4 Other CDL Rules

question: The International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) provide for equitable collection and distribution of fees and taxes for vehicles traveling through how many jurisdictions?
choice_a: The 48 contiguous United States and 10 Canadian provinces
choice_c: All of North America, including Mexico
explanation: The manual states IRP and IFTA provide for the equitable collection and distribution of vehicle license fees and motor fuels taxes for vehicles traveling throughout the 48 contiguous United States and 10 Canadian provinces.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.5 International Registration Plan / International Fuel Tax Agreement

question: What does IVDR stand for, as used in the IRP/IFTA record-keeping requirements?
explanation: The manual explains the IVDR, sometimes called a Driver Trip Report, is an Individual Vehicle Distance Record documenting distance traveled and fuel purchased.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.5 International Registration Plan / International Fuel Tax Agreement

question: IVDR records must be maintained for a minimum of how many years?
explanation: The manual states that original IVDR records, used to calculate fees and taxes payable to jurisdictions, must be maintained for a minimum of four years.
source_note: Kansas Commercial Driver's License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Kansas Department of Revenue Division of Vehicles -- Section 1, 1.5 International Registration Plan / International Fuel Tax Agreement
